title: A public record can be alive without being a diary
overview: Chronicle is moving toward timely decisions with enough context to understand what changed. Personal taste, private circumstances, and routine working details stay off the public page.
decision: Share the meaningful change and the open question. Keep the private story private.
question: How much context makes a decision useful without turning it into personal exposure?
basis: Ryan’s October 5 direction for the public Chronicle.

title: Human time is not a performance defect
overview: The public introduction now describes the difference between faster tools and the time people need to understand, trust, and change. An illustrative machine-versus-human chart gave way to a clearer statement.
decision: Keep the human constraint visible without presenting a metaphor as measured data.
question: How do we recognize useful acceleration without treating every slower human process as waste?
basis: Public homepage revision; editorial summary of the published change.

title: A boundary profile needs a test, not a promise
overview: Anti-Attachment now frames a portable profile as an instruction a person can carry between tools. Whether a model honors those instructions is a research question.
decision: Treat portability and actual compliance as separate things to evaluate.
question: Can the same profile reliably preserve uncertainty, boundaries, and decision authority across systems?
basis: Editorial summary of the current public Anti-Attachment project.

title: Reflection does not need a diagnostic score
overview: The human-boundary project keeps its reflection questions while removing unvalidated traffic-light scoring. The questions invite attention to habits without claiming to diagnose a person.
decision: Keep the prompts. Remove the unsupported measurement claim.
question: What evidence would be needed before any numerical agency measure should be trusted?
basis: Public project revision; editorial summary, not a claim of clinical validation.

title: SEER narrows to the operating decision
overview: The commercial work became clearer: start with a real business question, connect the minimum useful data and context, validate the result, and return an operating signal to the person responsible for the decision.
decision: Lead with measurable operating capability rather than a grand AI-system story.
question: Can the general approach be independently reproduced on clean data?
basis: Previously published Chronicle summary. Month-level dating retained.

title: Human Signal separates model behavior from human boundaries
overview: The research split into two related questions: what models do under defined conditions, and whether a person can carry explicit interaction boundaries across AI systems.
decision: Keep both as research tracks without claiming universal rankings, personality, or guaranteed enforcement.
question: Which boundaries will different systems actually respect?
basis: Previously published Chronicle summary. Month-level dating retained.

title: Convergence becomes an exploration, not a conclusion
overview: The worldview work shifted toward comparing what different lenses illuminate and what they may miss, while keeping fact, forecast, interpretation, and belief distinct.
decision: Preserve disagreement and give readers a simple on-ramp before deeper material.
question: Where do apparently similar interpretations genuinely disagree?
basis: Previously published Chronicle summary. Month-level dating retained.

title: SEE, R becomes the public umbrella
overview: Work, Christian formation, research, music, and experiments were brought into one public hub without forcing them into one product or one explanation.
decision: Use one front door while allowing each project to keep its own purpose.
question: How can each project remain understandable on its own?
basis: Previously published Chronicle summary. Month-level dating retained.
